doc.name: A — fragrance catalogue, chrome podium, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: eau de parfum flacon
Category: fragrance
Shot programme: chrome podium
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this fragrance product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the split-level stack in a chrome podium treatment.

SUBJECT. A eau de parfum flacon. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Product on a stepped plinth arrangement at two heights. Shoot on a 20mm wide at f/1.2, framing for diagonal dynamic balance across the frame.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with golden-hour backlight with heavy lens flare control. Stage the product on or against washed linen, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a neutral commercial grade with clean whites and no colour cast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
